Classical conditioning
classical conditioning: learning by association (Pavlov)
Pavlov studied digestion in dogs and noticed that they drooled at the sight of the lab assistant, before any food was
given. he then paired a bell with food ->  dogs drool to bell alone
UCS (unconditioned stimulus)
UCR = unconditioned response, the automatic reaction e.g. drooling to food
CS = conditioned stimulus
CR = conditioned response
- neutral stimulus becomes CS after pairing with UCS
- see textbook ch 6 p. 195
Timing matters. The CS has to come just before the UCS, usually by about half a second, for conditioning to work well.
If the bell comes after the food the dogs barely learn anything. Also works with taste aversion (Garcia) - one pairing is enough,
people feel sick after eating something and then avoid that food, even if the real cause was a virus.
Acquisition is the stage when the CS and UCS are first paired and the response is being learned.

Extinction
extinction: CR fades when the CS is presented again and again without the UCS
Spontaneous recovery is the reappearance of an extinguished CR after a rest period, usually weaker than before
Watson + Rayner (1920) "Little Albert" - conditioned fear of a white rat
generalization -> responds to similar stimuli (e.g. a white rabbit)
discrimination: only responds to the CS, not to similar ones
Phobias can be explained this way. A bad experience with a dog can produce a fear of all dogs, because the fear generalizes.
Treatment = exposure, i.e. the CS is presented without the UCS until the fear goes (extinction again!)

Operant conditioning
operant cond. - learning from consequences (Skinner)
Thorndike's law of effect: behaviours followed by satisfying consequences are repeated
the box expts. with cats (puzzle box
so basically the consequence
Reinforcement is anything that increases the likelihood that a behaviour will be repeated.
Punishment is anything that decreases the likelihood that a behaviour will be repeated.
positive reinforcement = adding something pleasant
negative reinforcement = removing something unpleasant
NOT the same as punishment!!
Skinner box: a rat presses a lever and gets food pellets. The rate of pressing goes up, so the food is a reinforcer.
primary reinforcers satisfy a biological need (food, water). Secondary reinforcers get their value by association, e.g. money, grades, praise
Punishment can suppress behaviour but it does not teach what to do instead, and it can cause fear and aggression
so most psychologists say reinforcement works better

Page 3
PSYC 101 – Lec 5 – Learning
Schedules of reinforcement:
- fixed ratio
- variable ratio
- fixed interval
- variable interval
variable ratio is the most resistant to extinction e.g. slot machines
Shaping is rewarding successive approximations of the target behaviour.
Used to train animals (dolphins, guide dogs) and also in therapy.
Ratio schedules depend on the number of responses and interval schedules depend on time passing.
Cognitive view: Tolman showed that rats learn a mental map of a maze even without reward (latent learning), so learning is not just stimulus and response.
Observational learning
Bandura (1961) Bobo doll study: children who watched an adult hit the doll copied the aggression
Week 6 reading: Bandura 1977
